narrative.overview: VaseraOS reads like a well-run back office, not a consumer app: calm, precise, unfussy. Every screen exists to be scanned fast and trusted — a resident roster, a dues ledger, a complaint queue — by people who range from a tech-fluent office bearer to a resident or guard who is not tech-savvy. The aesthetic stays simple and elegant on purpose, leaning on conventions people already know rather than novel interaction patterns, so it feels immediately familiar rather than clever. Confirmed anti-reference: not the bright, card-heavy, consumer-flashy look of MyGate/NoBrokerHood-style RWA apps. VaseraOS's edge is the guard-alarm pipeline, not decorative polish — so the interface is deliberately quiet everywhere except the one place urgency is real: the SOS alarm overlay.
keyCharacteristics: Zinc-neutral ink on white (and inverted in dark mode), one indigo accent, one red danger signal.
Flat, bordered surfaces by default; shadow is allowed on cards too, used to lift emphasis rather than as a default treatment.
A single consistent module-dot color per product area, repeated across home and admin dashboards.
One deliberate exception to the calm palette: the full-screen SOS alarm overlay, which goes loud because that moment is the product's whole reason to exist.

rules.name: The One Danger Rule
rules.body: Destructive or alarming UI uses red-*, never rose-*. UserMenu's logout control currently uses rose and is drift, not a second valid danger color.

rules.name: The One Dot Per Module Rule
rules.body: Each product module keeps exactly one identity color, used only as a small dot indicator — never promoted to a full background or button color.

rules.name: The Loud Exception Rule
rules.body: The SOS alarm overlay is the only screen allowed to break the system's calm register. Nothing else should use this intensity of color, blur, or motion.

dos: Do keep the palette near-monochrome everywhere except module dots and the SOS overlay.
Do use red-* for every destructive/danger surface — button, color, badge tone, banner.
Do default to a border for separation; reach for shadow only to lift a genuinely floating or emphasized surface.
Do favor familiar, conventional UI patterns over novel interaction design — the audience includes non-tech-savvy residents and guards.
Do keep exactly one identity color per module, expressed only as a small dot indicator.
donts: Don't use rose-* for destructive UI outside the SOS overlay — red-* is canonical; fix UserMenu's logout color rather than copying it elsewhere.
Don't add a second accent color; Ledger Indigo stays the only emphasis color outside module dots and the SOS overlay.
Don't give the SOS alarm overlay's intensity to any other screen.
Don't introduce decorative/novel UI patterns in pursuit of delight — simplicity and familiarity are the design goal for this audience.
